elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires Vendor to refund, on a pro rata basis, all prepaid Fees for the period after termination becomes effective.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly prohibits Vendor from terminating the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty days, not 60 to 90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee applies: Section 9.4 provides a refund, and the take-or-pay commitment in Section 2.1 is expressly subject to Section 9.4.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 bars Vendor convenience termination during a committed term, so any such termination could occur only outside that committed term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered language imposes no 90-day notice requirement on Vendor for any convenience termination outside a committed term.
